fields.v: Ayon, R. S. (2026). From Helpful to Trustworthy: LLM Agents for Pair Programming. In FSE Companion '26 (34th ACM Joint European Software Engineering Conference and Symposium on the Foundations of Software Engineering), Montreal, 2 pages. doi:10.1145/3803437.3804875. arXiv:2604.10300v1
Conference — FSE Companion '26, doctoral research paper (2 pages); read from arXiv copy
Academia: Texas State University (PhD student; advisor Shibbir Ahmed, Texas State University)

Proposes an approach; secondary: Conceptual — doctoral research plan proposing a driver-navigator multi-agent LLM pair-programming workflow with formal specifications and verifier feedback; summarises the author's prior results (AutoReSpec, AutoJML) but reports no new evaluation
fields.why: A specific driver-navigator workflow is proposed (p. 1), which fits 'Proposes an approach', but the paper is a two-page doctoral plan with one paragraph of design and no evaluation, so 'Conceptual' as main nature is also defensible. Q13 applies either way.

fields.v: Driver-navigator multi-agent LLM pair-programming workflow (unnamed, proposed); builds on the author's AutoReSpec (verifier-guided JML synthesis) and AutoJML (ReAct agents for JML). No versions

Standards-aligned requirements; machine-checkable contracts and formal specifications (e.g., JML) produced by the navigator; tests; implementations; solver-backed counterexamples/proofs as auditable evidence; shared persistent project context

Planned three studies/stages: (1) informal problem statement -> standards-aligned requirements and formal specifications; (2) refine tests and implementations with automated feedback (SMT counterexamples, TDD); (3) maintenance (refactoring, API migration, documentation) constrained by existing specs and tests. Within each: driver proposes, navigator critiques via formal specs, deterministic verifiers return proofs or counterexamples
